title: Event assertions can bind to pre-existing matching events
reasoning: The fixture creates a USER_JOINED_FAST event before test_fast_join_signal runs, then the test triggers another USER_JOINED_FAST event and retrieves an arbitrary matching row with .first(). Because multiple rows can match the same event_type/user/target, the assertion may inspect the setup event instead of the newly emitted signal event, making the test order-dependent and weakening its ability to catch signal regressions.
recommendation: Capture the event IDs present before the action, then assert against Event.objects.exclude(id__in=existing_ids) or order by descending timestamp/id and verify the event count plus the new row explicitly.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The test checks the count increment, but the detailed assertions are made against an unscoped query that can return an older matching event.
suggestedRegressionTest: Modify test_fast_join_signal so it records existing USER_JOINED_FAST IDs before self.profile.fasts.add(self.fast), then asserts exactly one new join event exists and the feed item references that new event.
minimumFixScope: Constrain the query in test_fast_join_signal to the event created by the action under test.
